clue.text: Time for wild party at swine's place? It's nothing like that!

parts.note: a rave is a wild all-night party
a sty is where pigs are kept

explanation.surface: A rowdy all-night party held in a pigpen is dismissed as nothing like the real thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads off the scene: a travesty is a grotesque imitation, nothing like what it mocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a distorted parody bearing little resemblance to the real thing it imitates.

clue.text: See 15
See 22
The "Lily Maid" is in denial except when climbing

indicators.note: when climbing says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Tennyson's Lily Maid is in a state of denial except when she climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'when climbing' reads the run upwards; 'in' marks the letters sitting inside 'denial except'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaine of Astolat is called the Lily Maid in Arthurian legend and Tennyson's Idylls of the King.

clue.text: After the endless dance I need a hip replacement: defy me at your peril!

indicators.note: After places the dance straight behind the shortened word, in answer order
endless says the word is cut short by losing its final letter

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
taken as written
a replacement hip is a new hip

explanation.surface: A patient who has worn out a hip dancing warns everyone not to cross them.
explanation.walkthrough: A three-line whip is the strictest order a British party gives its MPs to vote its way; defying it risks expulsion. 'need' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A party instruction underlined three times that members disobey at serious risk to their careers.

clue.text: Swine's flesh eaten by group that's sent back flower

indicators.note: eaten by puts the meat inside the other piece, as food goes inside a mouth
sent back says the word for group is read in reverse

parts.note: a set is a group
ham is meat from a pig

explanation.surface: Pork is consumed by a party that returns a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword's flow-er, a river: here London's river.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that flows, so crosswords call one a flower; this is England's best-known river.

clue.text: Homo sapiens chasing swine, a year's beginning — and end

indicators.note: chasing puts the human after the pig, following it in answer order

parts.note: a hog is a pig
Homo sapiens is man, the human species

indicators.note: a beginning is the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Human beings chase pigs at the start and finish of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' puts MAN behind HOG. The definition 'end' reads on from 'a year's': Hogmanay is the Scottish New Year's Eve, the year's last day.
explanation.definitionFit: Hogmanay, the Scottish celebration on 31 December, marks the final day of the old year.

clue.text: Semi-simultaneous disaster for Conservative at car park

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in a mess, so the letters are scrambled
Semi- means half, so only the first half of the long word is used

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A half-simultaneous calamity befalls a Tory at a car park.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of 'simultaneous' is SIMULT, which 'disaster' turns into MULTIS.
explanation.definitionFit: A multi-level parking garage is the commonest kind of building with many floors.

clue.text: Opening word to selected player or oil producer

parts.note: 'Open sesame' is the magic word that opens the cave in Ali Baba
a seed is a player ranked in advance in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: A password is offered to a ranked player, or to someone who makes oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Sesame seeds are pressed to give sesame oil, so the seed produces oil.

clue.text: Actor's reversal of purpose to produce swine

indicators.note: reversal of says the word for purpose is turned backwards

parts.note: an aim is a purpose
to farrow is for a sow to give birth to piglets

explanation.surface: A performer claims that turning purpose around makes pigs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor's' is 'Actor is': Mia Farrow is the American film actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Mia Farrow is an American film performer, famous for Rosemary's Baby.

clue.text: Left 4, in digital terms, bothered Fringe after union takeover

indicators.note: after sets the scrambled word behind the union, in answer order

parts.note: a wedding is a union, a merger in which each partner takes the other on

indicators.note: bothered means flustered, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: The Edinburgh Fringe is troubled after a trade union seizes control.
explanation.walkthrough: Fingers are digits: the ring finger is the fourth of the left hand counting the thumb. FINGER is an anagram of FRINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: The fourth digit of the left hand is traditionally where a married person wears the ring.

clue.text: Red stickers need little internal change

indicators.note: a small change inside the word means one letter shifts its place within it

parts.note: glues are things that make objects stick

explanation.surface: Red stickers only want a small alteration inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the L and U of GLUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Gules is the heraldic term for the colour red on a coat of arms.

clue.text: What's resulting in cinders? I am

definitions.text: What's resulting in cinders? I am

indicators.note: the answer is what results when these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asked what leaves cinders behind, the arsonist confesses.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay at once: the letters of IN CINDERS I AM rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiarism is arson, the deliberate setting of fires that leave ashes.

clue.text: Drink round through rip-off: it goes to the last

indicators.note: round says the drink is wrapped about the other letters

parts.note: booze is alcoholic drink
by can mean through, as in 'by way of'

indicators.note: off signals the three letters going wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink served round after a swindle, and it is awarded to whoever finishes bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rip-off' looks like one noun, a swindle; split it, RIP jumbled by 'off' gives PRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A booby prize is a joke award presented to the competitor who comes last.

clue.text: Cut name for swine, say, that will rush up river

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: say signals that the word for a male pig is used for its sound

parts.note: a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: Someone is told to cut out the name given to a pig, a beast that charges upstream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn bore is a tidal wave that surges up the River Severn in western England.
explanation.definitionFit: A tidal bore is a wave that travels upstream; the Severn's is Britain's largest.

clue.text: More work? That's clear to us in more than one case

parts.note: overt means open, plain to see

parts.words: us in more than one case
parts.note: the first person speaking in two grammatical cases: I as subject, ME as object

explanation.surface: Someone asks if there is extra work and is told the matter is plain in several instances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is grammatical: the speaker is I in the nominative and ME in the accusative.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtime is extra hours worked beyond the normal working day.

clue.text: Self-appointed police given tails for disguise

indicators.note: a disguise changes how something looks, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Unofficial lawmen are handed tails to wear as a costume.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigilantes are citizens who take law enforcement into their own hands without authority.

clue.text: Rise of Free Church over turn to the left in good spirits

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts one piece above the other
rise means the word goes up, read backwards in a down clue

parts.note: the word itself, before it is turned
a U-turn, so U is a turn

explanation.surface: The rise of the Free Church after a leftward shift has believers happy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Rise of' reads FREE upwards, and 'over' puts the church above it; 'to the' is a link before the abbreviation for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cheerful is being happy and upbeat in mood.

clue.text: It's nice to go round the garden with a busy companion and not make decisions

definitions.text: It's nice to go round the garden

parts.note: busy as a bee: the bee is the proverbial busy creature
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order
to hedge is to avoid committing oneself

explanation.surface: A pleasant garden stroll with a bustling friend who will not decide anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a garden boundary: a hedge of beech round the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedge of beech trees is a popular, attractive boundary planting enclosing a garden.

clue.text: Cheese is shorter than short

indicators.note: shorter than means the word for short loses a letter from its end

parts.note: brief means short

explanation.surface: A cheese is called briefer than brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft French cheese with a white rind.

clue.text: Sphere in which to commit matricide

parts.note: to commit a killing is to do someone in
matricide is killing one's mother, MA
the in of 'do in', placed after the victim

explanation.surface: A realm in which someone kills their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: To commit matricide is to 'do Ma in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a field or area of activity, a sphere of influence.

clue.text: God etc off to the borders of heaven with picture that's for removal

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are jumbled
the borders are the outer letters of the word

parts.note: an icon is a sacred picture

explanation.surface: A deity and his extras head off to heaven's edge with a painting to be moved.
explanation.walkthrough: ETC jumbled gives TEC; heaven's borders are H and N. A pantechnicon is a British term for a large furniture-removal van.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantechnicon is a large van used for moving house furniture.

clue.text: Abandon with a stroke of the pen, for example: I'm like a rodent inside

definitions.text: Abandon with a stroke of the pen

indicators.note: inside puts the rodent phrase within the word for example

parts.note: say means for example
rodents gnaw, so the speaker says I GNAW

explanation.surface: Giving up rights by signature, for example, makes someone feel like a rat inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign away something is to give it up by signing a document.

clue.text: Precipitation is, for swine, about the end of it

annotationWithheld.why: Precipitation is, for swine, about the end of it (4): SOW around N, but N is the last letter of 'Precipitation', the definition, so that word does two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Precipitation is, for swine, about the end of it

clue.text: Start of harmless shot at billiards

indicators.note: only the opening of the synonym is kept, the rest cut away

parts.note: inoffensive means harmless

explanation.surface: The opening of a harmless stroke on the billiard table.
explanation.walkthrough: An in-off is a billiards shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards an in-off is a stroke where the cue ball enters a pocket after striking another ball.

clue.text: Swine heard to master predator with mythical sculptor

indicators.note: heard means the word for swine is taken by its sound

parts.note: a pig is a swine
MA is a Master of Arts
a lion is a predator

explanation.surface: A pig was heard to overpower a hunting beast with a legendary sculptor present.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Pygmalion was a sculptor who fell in love with his own statue.

clue.text: Change diarist John's name's place in a regular way

indicators.note: Change ... place says one letter shifts to another position in the word
the place being changed is the position of the letter for name

parts.note: John Evelyn was a 17th-century English diarist
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A diarist's name is moved to another spot in a neat way.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the N of EVELYN two places to give EVENLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenly means uniformly, at a steady and regular rate.

clue.text: Refuse to go back — that's a first

parts.note: bran is husk, the refuse of milled grain

indicators.note: back says the word for go is read in reverse

parts.note: to wend is to go

explanation.surface: Declining to return is described as unprecedented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb but is the noun, waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brand new has never been used or seen before, a novelty or first.
